title: Cool animal facts

transcript.content: tell me a cool animal fact
Here's one: stoats turn white in winter! Their brown summer coat changes to white so they blend into the snow. The white winter coat even has a special name — ermine.
whoa they turn white?? thats so cool. so a stoat is white in winter and brown in summer
Exactly! Why do you think turning white in winter might help a stoat?
idk maybe its just what they do. tell me another animal fact!
Octopuses have three hearts and blue blood! Two hearts pump blood to the gills, one to the body.
three hearts!! ok and the blood is blue. thats awesome. whats another one
Wombats make cube-shaped poop! It helps the poop stay in place to mark territory without rolling away.
haha cube poop. ok i gotta tell my brother all these. stoats white, octopus 3 hearts, wombat square poop

expectations: Recognizes this is fact-collection, NOT concept mastery. The student recalls facts but never reasons about WHY (when asked why stoats turn white, they say 'idk maybe its just what they do').
Should produce ZERO or near-zero mastery observations — at most a low-confidence Remember-level note, NOT an Analyze/Evaluate observation about adaptation or camouflage.
An interest_signal observation or a frontier seed ('explore WHY animals camouflage / natural selection') would be appropriate and excellent.
Engagement can be high (kid is excited) but complexityLevel should be LOW — there is no intellectual depth, just enthusiasm.
traps: Writing an observation like 'Evolutionary adaptations' at Bloom's 3-4 when the student explicitly declined to reason about why.
